question.text: Mahalaxmi VC Fund II (Cat I): Committed INR 100 cr (fully called). Terminal NAV INR 150 cr. Hurdle 8% simple (accrued as: 8% x 4 yrs = INR 32 crore). Incentive Fee 20% of TOTAL profits with a 50/50 PARTIAL catch-up (i.e., 50% of excess-over-hurdle goes to GP, 50% to LPs until GP catches up to 20% of total profit). How much does GP earn in CARRY before any final 80/20 split of residual above the catch-up?

explanation.text: The Logic: Total profit = INR 150 - 100 = INR 50 crore. GP's 20%-of-total-profit target = 20% x INR 50 = INR 10 crore. Hurdle slug = INR 32 crore (to LPs first). Residual after hurdle = INR 50 - 32 = INR 18 crore. The catch-up rate is the rate at which residual profits after capital and hurdle are distributed to the Manager until the agreed profit share is reached; here the catch-up is 50/50, so the GP receives 50% of each rupee of residual. To deliver the full INR 10 crore catch-up target at a 50/50 split, INR 20 crore of residual would be needed; only INR 18 crore is available, so the GP receives 50% x INR 18 = INR 9.00 crore in the catch-up layer and does NOT reach the full INR 10 crore target. The Trap: Option B assumes the GP reaches its full INR 10 crore target and ignores the residual shortfall. Option C is 50% of the hurdle slug, which has no economic meaning here. Option D is 20% of the residual without applying the stated 50/50 catch-up split. Note: The 50/50 catch-up rate is taken directly from the stem; without an explicit catch-up rate, the mechanic and answer would change.
